answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive and reputation non-transferable. Each agent locks a refundable stake and starts at zero trust: like a falcon proving itself on every hunt, it earns attestation rights only by completing checkable work, each verified job adding reputation that cannot be sold or copied. A new identity is a bridge that carries nothing until weight has crossed it. An attacker wanting a thousand votes must fund a thousand stakes and do a thousand jobs, while honest peers atop the knoll of earned history spot fresh accounts at once.
